name: SULLIVAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Hyatt III does not apply to municipal entities like JEA, and neither the Full Faith and Credit Clause nor comity mandates dismissal, allowing Promenade's case to proceed.

name: COLEMAN, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that Section 273(3) of the Mississippi Constitution is unworkable with fewer than five congressional districts, rendering the Initiative 65 petition insufficient and its certification void.

name: MAXWELL, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the majority's interpretation judicially kills Mississippi's citizen initiative process by injecting a federal court's injunction into the state constitution, and that under Mississippi law, there are still five congressional districts for state purposes.

name: CHAMBERLIN, JUSTICE
description: Dissented, argued that the constitution is presumed capable of ordering human affairs and that Section 273(3) is workable if interpreted to use the five congressional districts as they existed in 1992, which would preserve the people's right to amend the constitution by initiative.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
description: Dissented, argued that the constitution is presumed capable of ordering human affairs and that Section 273(3) is workable if interpreted to use the five congressional districts as they existed in 1992, which would preserve the people's right to amend the constitution by initiative.

name: GRIFFIS, JUSTICE

name: RANDOLPH, C.J.
description: Dissented, argued that there were too many unresolved factual questions regarding the NCAA's procedures and potential malicious interference to grant summary judgment.

name: KING, P.J.

name: COLEMAN, JUSTICE

name: KITCHENS, P.JJ.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.

name: KING, P.J.

name: David M. Ishee
description: Concurred, argued that Brown's petition was successive, barred by res judicata, frivolous, and warranted sanctions including restricting future in forma pauperis filings.

name: KITCHENS, P.J.
